shorts.title: The Great Emu War
shorts.covers: In 1932 the Australian army sent soldiers with machine guns to fight emus eating Western Australia's wheat, and the emus won.
shorts.source: Australian newspaper archives (Trove) and military histories of the 1932 operation

shorts.title: The War That Lasted 38 Minutes
shorts.covers: On 27 August 1896 Britain and Zanzibar fought the shortest war on record, over who would become sultan.
shorts.source: Standard histories of the Anglo-Zanzibar War

shorts.title: The Christmas Truce of 1914
shorts.covers: On Christmas 1914 British and German soldiers on the Western Front climbed out of their trenches, shook hands, swapped gifts and buried their dead.
shorts.source: Soldiers' letters published by the Imperial War Museum and histories of the truce

shorts.title: Saragarhi: 21 Soldiers at the Fort
shorts.covers: On 12 September 1897, 21 Sikh soldiers held a signalling post on the North-West Frontier against thousands of Pashtun tribesmen, to the last man.
shorts.source: British Indian Army records and histories of the 36th Sikhs

shorts.title: The Soldier Who Fought On for 29 Years
shorts.covers: Hiroo Onoda, a Japanese officer, kept fighting in the Philippine jungle until 1974, because nobody he trusted had told him the war was over.
shorts.source: Onoda's memoir No Surrender and contemporary reporting

shorts.title: The Great Molasses Flood
shorts.covers: In January 1919 a giant tank burst in Boston and a wave of molasses swept through the streets, killing 21 people.
shorts.source: Stephen Puleo's Dark Tide and Boston newspaper archives

shorts.title: The London Beer Flood
shorts.covers: In 1814 a huge vat burst at a London brewery and over a million litres of beer flooded the slum of St Giles, killing eight people.
shorts.source: Contemporary London newspapers and histories of the Horse Shoe Brewery

shorts.title: The Pig War
shorts.covers: In 1859 an American farmer shot a British pig on an island near Canada, and two empires sent warships. The only casualty was the pig.
shorts.source: US National Park Service history of San Juan Island

shorts.title: The Pope Put on Trial After Death
shorts.covers: In 897 Pope Stephen VI had the body of his predecessor, Formosus, dug up, dressed and put on trial: the Cadaver Synod.
shorts.source: Liudprand of Cremona and standard histories of the papacy

shorts.title: Operation Mincemeat
shorts.covers: In 1943 British intelligence floated a dead man with fake secret papers off the coast of Spain to fool Germany about where the Allies would invade.
shorts.source: Ewen Montagu's account and Ben Macintyre's Operation Mincemeat

shorts.title: The Ghost Army
shorts.covers: In 1944 a US unit of artists and sound engineers used inflatable tanks and fake radio traffic to fool the German army.
shorts.source: US Army records and histories of the 23rd Headquarters Special Troops

shorts.title: The Night Witches
shorts.covers: Soviet women pilots flew old wooden biplanes on night bombing raids from 1942, gliding in with their engines off.
shorts.source: Memoirs of the 588th Night Bomber Regiment and histories of Soviet women in WWII

shorts.title: Mansa Musa: The Richest Pilgrim
shorts.covers: In 1324 the king of Mali crossed the Sahara to Mecca with so much gold that he changed its price in Cairo for years.
shorts.source: Al-Umari's account and histories of the Mali Empire

shorts.title: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi
shorts.covers: In 1858 the queen of Jhansi fought the East India Company's army herself, and died in battle near Gwalior.
shorts.source: Histories of the 1857 uprising and British military dispatches

shorts.title: The Salt March
shorts.covers: In 1930 Gandhi walked 240 miles to the sea to make a handful of salt, and broke the British salt law in front of the world.
shorts.source: Histories of the Indian independence movement and contemporary reporting

shorts.title: The Halifax Explosion
shorts.covers: On 6 December 1917 a ship full of explosives blew up in Halifax harbour in Canada, the largest man-made blast before the atomic bomb.
shorts.source: Nova Scotia Archives and histories of the explosion

shorts.title: Tulip Mania
shorts.covers: In 1637 a single tulip bulb in the Netherlands could sell for more than a house, until one day nobody would buy.
shorts.source: Anne Goldgar's Tulipmania, which also corrects the popular myths

shorts.title: The Great Fire of London
shorts.covers: In September 1666 a fire from a bakery on Pudding Lane burned for four days and destroyed most of the City of London.
shorts.source: The diaries of Samuel Pepys and John Evelyn

shorts.title: Hannibal's Elephants Cross the Alps
shorts.covers: In 218 BCE the Carthaginian general Hannibal led an army with elephants over the Alps to attack Rome from the north.
shorts.source: Polybius and Livy

shorts.title: Thrown From a Window in Prague
shorts.covers: In 1618 Protestant nobles threw two Catholic officials out of a castle window in Prague; they survived, and the Thirty Years' War began.
shorts.source: Peter Wilson's Europe's Tragedy and contemporary accounts

shorts.title: The Trung Sisters' Revolt
shorts.covers: In 40 CE two sisters led Vietnam's uprising against Chinese rule and ruled as queens for three years.
shorts.source: Vietnamese and Chinese histories of the Han period

shorts.title: Thermopylae: More Than 300
shorts.covers: In 480 BCE a small Greek force, led by 300 Spartans, held a narrow pass against the Persian army of Xerxes for three days.
shorts.source: Herodotus and modern histories of the Persian Wars

shorts.title: The Charge of the Light Brigade
shorts.covers: In 1854 a confused order sent British cavalry charging straight down a valley of Russian guns in the Crimean War.
shorts.source: Contemporary dispatches, William Howard Russell's reports, and histories of Balaclava

shorts.title: The Warship That Sank in Minutes
shorts.covers: In 1628 Sweden's mightiest warship, the Vasa, sailed about 1,300 metres on her first voyage and sank in Stockholm harbour.
shorts.source: The Vasa Museum's history and the 1628 inquiry records

shorts.title: The Night He Did Nothing
shorts.covers: In 1983 a Soviet officer, Stanislav Petrov, saw his screens report incoming American missiles and decided it was a false alarm.
shorts.source: Interviews with Petrov and histories of the 1983 false alarm

shorts.title: The Peacock Throne Leaves Delhi
shorts.covers: In 1739 the Persian ruler Nader Shah sacked Delhi and carried off the Mughal Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.
shorts.source: Histories of Nader Shah's invasion and William Dalrymple and Anita Anand's Koh-i-Noor

shorts.title: The Great Siege of Malta
shorts.covers: In 1565 a few thousand Knights of St John and Maltese defenders held their island against a huge Ottoman fleet for nearly four months.
shorts.source: Francisco Balbi di Correggio's diary and Ernle Bradford's The Great Siege

shorts.title: The Radium Girls
shorts.covers: In the 1920s young women painting glowing watch dials were told to lick their brushes, and their fight for justice changed workers' rights.
shorts.source: Kate Moore's The Radium Girls and the court records

shorts.title: The Children's Crusade
shorts.covers: In 1212 crowds of young people in France and Germany set off to take Jerusalem, and historians still argue about what really happened.
shorts.source: The medieval chronicles and Gary Dickson's The Children's Crusade

shorts.title: The Man Who Volunteered for Auschwitz
shorts.covers: In 1940 a Polish officer, Witold Pilecki, let himself be arrested so he could get inside Auschwitz and report what was happening there.
shorts.source: Pilecki's reports (published as The Auschwitz Volunteer) and Jack Fairweather's The Volunteer
